article.title: AI Incident Response Needs a Human Escalation Path
article.author: OpenAI learning editor
article.why: AI 事故管理需要把技術調查、停止權限、法務風險與人類責任串成同一條 escalation path。

paragraphs.en:
When an AI system behaves badly in production, the response cannot be limited to debugging the model. An AI incident may affect customers, employees, data, compliance obligations, or business decisions before engineers fully understand the technical cause. Organizations therefore need a human escalation path that connects technical investigation with operational authority.

The first step is to define what counts as an incident. A single strange answer from a chatbot may be a minor quality problem, while repeated disclosure of confidential information is much more serious. Other examples include harmful recommendations, discriminatory outcomes, unexpected automation of high-impact decisions, major drops in model performance, or a system using data outside its approved purpose. Clear severity levels help teams respond consistently instead of debating urgency during a crisis.

Ownership is equally important. Engineers can investigate logs, prompts, model versions, retrieval results, and recent deployment changes. They may not have authority to stop a customer-facing service, notify legal teams, or communicate with affected users. A documented escalation path should therefore name who can pause the system, who evaluates legal or privacy risk, who coordinates business operations, and who approves restoration.

Logging supports that process. Teams need enough evidence to reconstruct what happened: the model and configuration used, relevant inputs and outputs, tool calls, retrieved documents, policy decisions, timestamps, and changes made shortly before the incident. Logs must themselves be governed carefully because they may contain sensitive data. The goal is not to record everything forever, but to preserve the information needed for diagnosis and accountability.

A good response process also separates containment from root-cause analysis. During an active incident, the fastest safe action may be to disable one feature, route requests to a human, restrict a tool, or roll back a recent change. The team can investigate the deeper cause after exposure is controlled. Waiting for perfect technical certainty before containing a serious risk can increase harm.

Human escalation is especially important for systems that operate across organizational boundaries. A model may be technically maintained by one team, embedded in a product owned by another, and supported by an external vendor. Without predefined contacts and decision rights, each group may assume someone else is responsible. Incident exercises can expose these gaps before a real failure occurs.

After recovery, the organization should review both the technical cause and the response process. Did monitoring detect the problem quickly? Was severity classified correctly? Did the right people receive enough information? Could anyone stop the system? Were customers or internal users informed appropriately? The answers often reveal governance weaknesses that are not visible in normal model evaluation.

AI incident response is therefore a socio-technical discipline. Model quality matters, but so do authority, communication, evidence, and business continuity. A robust system is not one that never fails. It is one whose organization can recognize failure, limit its impact, learn from it, and restore service under clear human responsibility.

Teams can make this practical with a short incident playbook. The playbook should list severity criteria, emergency contacts, evidence to capture, temporary controls, communication channels, and restoration conditions. It should also specify when an incident must be escalated outside the product team. Regular tabletop exercises are useful because they test whether people can actually follow the process under time pressure. A policy that exists only in a document is weaker than a process that teams have rehearsed.
paragraphs.zh: AI 系統在 production 出問題時，不能只 debug model，因為影響可能先擴及客戶、員工、資料、法遵與商業決策。組織需要一條把技術調查與營運權限連起來的 human escalation path。第一步是定義 incident 與 severity：偶發怪答案可能只是輕微品質問題，持續洩漏機密、有害建議、歧視性結果、高影響決策被意外自動化、模型表現大幅下降或使用未核准資料，都需要不同級別處理。Ownership 也要事先清楚。工程師可以查 logs、prompts、模型版本與 deployment 變更，但不一定有權停止服務、通知法務或對使用者溝通，因此必須明定誰能 pause system、誰判斷 legal/privacy risk、誰協調營運、誰批准 restoration。Logging 則應保留足以重建事件的模型設定、輸入輸出、tool calls、retrieved documents、policy decisions、時間戳與近期變更，同時治理 log 內的敏感資料。好的 response 會把 containment 與 root-cause analysis 分開；事故進行中可以先關閉 feature、轉人工、限制 tool 或 rollback，再深入找根因，而不是等到百分之百確定才控制風險。跨團隊與 vendor 的 AI 更需要預先定義 contacts 與 decision rights。恢復後也要 review 偵測速度、severity 分類、資訊傳遞、停止權限與通知是否有效。AI incident response 是 socio-technical discipline：穩健不是永遠不失敗，而是能辨認、限制、學習並在清楚的人類責任下恢復。短 playbook 與定期 tabletop exercise 可以把這套治理變成真正可執行的流程。
paragraphs.ja: AIが本番で問題を起こしたとき、モデルのデバッグだけでは不十分です。影響が顧客、従業員、データ、コンプライアンス、事業判断へ先に広がる可能性があるため、技術調査と業務権限を結ぶ人間のエスカレーション経路が必要です。まずインシデントと重大度を定義します。単発の不自然な回答と、機密情報の反復漏えい、有害推奨、差別的結果、高影響判断の予期しない自動化、性能急落、未承認データ利用では対応が異なります。責任も明確にし、誰が停止できるか、誰が法務・プライバシーリスクを評価するか、誰が業務を調整し、誰が復旧を承認するかを決めます。ログにはモデル設定、入出力、ツール呼び出し、検索文書、ポリシー判断、時刻、直近変更など、再現に必要な証拠を残しつつ、ログ自体の機密性も管理します。対応では封じ込めと根本原因分析を分け、必要なら機能停止、人への切替、ツール制限、ロールバックを先に実施します。複数チームや外部ベンダーが関わる場合は連絡先と意思決定権を事前に決める必要があります。復旧後は検知速度、重大度分類、情報共有、停止権限、利用者通知もレビューします。AIインシデント対応は社会技術的な仕事であり、堅牢性とは失敗しないことではなく、失敗を認識し、影響を限定し、学習し、人間の明確な責任のもとで復旧できることです。短いプレイブックと定期的な机上演習で、文書上の方針を実行可能なプロセスへ変えます。
